B. The product contains 94% of one enantiomer and 6% of the other enantiomer
C. The product contains 97% of one enantiomer and 3% of the other enantiomer
D. The product contains an enantiomer which is 94% pure

Thought: To solve this problem, I need to understand what enantiomeric excess (ee) means. Enantiomeric excess is a measure of the purity of an enantiomer in a mixture, defined as the absolute difference in the percentage of the two enantiomers. If a mixture has 94% enantiomeric excess, it means that there is a 94% excess of one enantiomer over the racemic mixture (which would be 50/50 of each enantiomer). Therefore, the correct interpretation of 94% enantiomeric excess would be that the product contains 97% of one enantiomer and 3% of the other enantiomer (since 94% is the excess over the 50% point, leading to 97% of one and 3% of the other).
